(i) we trained two deep nets from the ground-up to communicate about object categories through a largely interpretable protocol; (ii) the emergent protocol allowed the nets to communicate about object types not seen at training time; and (iii) the visual representations that emerged in the process, when used as generic visual features in a separate task, showed quality comparable to state-of-the-art self-supervised learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we train two deep networks to communicate about objects in a visual scene, and that the resulting visual representations are as good as those learned by state-of-the-art unsupervised visual learning methods.
we show the emergence of a communication protocol from scratch, and that the induced visual features are of high quality.

we have trained deep neural networks to perform referent communication from scratch, and in the process we have obtained a generic visual representation that is on par with state of the art self-supervised models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interpretable emergent communication is a promising way to bootstrap communication between deep nets.
the problem of emergent communication is not only interesting from a theoretical perspective but can also be used in practice to obtain interpretable communication and generic visual representations.
